#AISecurity #CyberSecurity
items.ig_caption:
One shared ChatGPT link. Your private chats. 🔗

What researchers at Parameter found (published 28 Oct):
→ A malicious shared ChatGPT link could run attacker code in a signed-in viewer's session
→ In one version, just opening the link was enough
→ Their proof listed recent chats, opened a private chat never shared with them and sent part of it to an outside server
→ They used test accounts; no real-world exploitation was reported
→ Reported 18 Oct, fixed 26 Oct, rated P1 (OpenAI's most serious category), $5,000 bounty

What to do: nothing to install, the fix is server-side. The lesson: an AI chat history is a data store. Treat unexpected shared links like any other link, and keep secrets out of chats.

items.send_to: anyone who applied for Florida aid

cover.hook: 4.9 million financial aid applicants. Social Security numbers exposed.
cover.sub: Florida's Department of Education says an unauthorised party got into its Student Financial Aid site. The site is down.

slides.title: What happened
slides.body: The Florida Department of Education says an unauthorised party gained access to a system or database behind its Student Financial Aid website. It learned of it on 19 Oct and announced it on 29 Oct. The site has been taken down.

slides.label: people who applied for financial aid in Florida
slides.note: Per the Florida Department of Education, via The Record

slides.title: What was exposed
slides.body: Names, addresses, phone numbers, genders, email addresses, Social Security numbers and dates of birth. The department hasn't said how the attackers got in or who they are. It says aid, tuition and loan payments won't be delayed.

slides.title: Why it matters
slides.body: SSN plus date of birth is the kit for opening credit in someone's name. Many applicants are students who have never checked a credit report. The state is urging people to watch their credit and accounts. No credit monitoring offer was mentioned.

slides.title: Do this week
items: Freeze your credit with all three US bureaus
Check your credit reports for unknown accounts
Expect phishing that mentions financial aid
Help a student in your family do the same

items.ig_caption:
3 Ivanti flaws. Chained to root. No login needed. 🚨

What's happening with Ivanti Connect Secure:
→ Attackers chained CVE-2026-104935 (auth bypass), CVE-2026-111357 and CVE-2026-118527 to get unauthenticated root
→ Volexity documented the chain and attributes it to a previously undocumented actor it calls UTA0576
→ No web shells or malware: the actor pulled credentials and Active Directory metadata, and searched for admin passwords and BitLocker recovery keys
→ CISA added two of the flaws to its exploited list on 30 Oct; the federal deadline for CVE-2026-111357 is 2 Nov

What to do: update to 25.1.1.3 or 22.8R2.6 (or later), rotate credentials that passed through the appliance, and check for BitLocker key access.

x_thread:
Binance hack: the FBI says North Korea's TraderTraitor stole about $6.3B, and asked exchanges and DeFi services to block 600+ laundering addresses. Same group linked to the $1.5B Bybit hack.

The week's lessons 🧵 #CryptoHack #CyberSecurity

1/ Timeline: Binance was hit on Thursday 30 Oct. On Saturday the FBI, with the Secret Service and IRS-CI, named "TraderTraitor actors" and listed 600+ Ethereum, ~20 Bitcoin and 1 Solana laundering address (CoinDesk).

2/ The way in, per Binance's early findings: a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, used to reach a service container and submit withdrawals. It later found more points of breach: "not a single 'one-click' action". No evidence private keys leaked.

3/ The money: converted mainly into ether, with DeFi and swap services expected next (FBI). Stablecoin issuers froze $2.4B+ (CoinDesk). Binance says it replaced ~90% with its own funds and will cover all losses.

4/ Same week, same pattern: attackers went after the people and tools with access, not the vault. A Pentagon-network AI agent allegation, a trojanized Claude Code extension, and Northflank telling customers to assume every secret was decrypted.

5/ Do this week: treat engineer laptops that reach prod as tier-0; require a second approver for high-value transfers; if you run a crypto service, block the FBI-listed addresses; rehearse a full freeze before you need one.

6/ Question: if one engineer's laptop were stolen tonight, what could it reach in production?

Sources: CoinDesk (31 Oct), ABC News (1 Nov), The Hacker News (30 Oct).

#SupplyChain #CyberSecurity
items.ig_caption:
A hidden circuit board. With its own antenna. Inside a hardware wallet. 🔍

What Trezor warned (30 Oct):
→ A customer reported a Trezor Safe 5, bought from reseller CryptoBilis, with an extra board between the main board and the screen
→ Per the report it has a cellular module and antenna, reads the screen (including the recovery phrase) and transmits it when plugged in
→ Trezor hasn't examined the device yet but warned buyers now: "Waiting for lab confirmation would leave CryptoBilis buyers exposed"
→ Trezor dropped CryptoBilis as a reseller on 9 Oct; Ledger is investigating losses among its own CryptoBilis buyers
→ No CryptoBilis buyer has reported lost funds to Trezor

What to do: if your wallet came from CryptoBilis, move funds to a new wallet with a new recovery phrase. Don't set up an unused one. Buy hardware only from official stores.
